discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 091933
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
233 PM EST Mon Nov 9 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Remaining dry with above normal temperatures into Tuesday.

- A chance for rain (40-70%) late Wednesday into Thursday.

- Cooler weather and lingering chances for lake effect showers into 
  Thursday night and Friday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 210 PM EST Mon Nov 9 2026

Mild weather will continue through Tuesday with slightly above
normal temperatures and dry conditions due to a large surface
high pushing up from the south. Mostly clear skies tonight will
allow temperatures to fall into the lower 40s. It will not be
quite as cold as last night since southwest winds will
contribute to better boundary layer mixing. This should also
keep fog and frost from forming. Winds will diminish
considerable though by Tuesday night to near calm, and
radiational cooling will drop temperatures into the mid 30s. The
HRRR is also indicating a large area of dense fog developing
across the region on Wednesday morning, which may require
advisories.

A deep trough then moves across the Midwest on Wednesday,
bringing rain to the local area by late afternoon and evening.
The accompanying cold front will also bring breezy north winds
going into Thursday. This northerly flow will result in lake
effect rain showers, and then possibly snow showers on Thursday
night and Friday. Right now it is too early to tell exactly how
much snow will fall, but with the recent warm weather, roadways
should stay warm enough for little to no accumulation. While it
will remain cool on Friday, temps will rise into the low 40s, 
causing subsequent melting. Showers should taper off on Saturday
as the large scale low advects farther east of the region and 
high pressure builds back in from the west. Dry weather is then 
expected on Sunday and Monday with gradually warming 
temperatures. Mondays highs are forecast to be back in the mid 
50s again. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 1226 PM EST Mon Nov 9 2026

VFR conditions will prevail with only a few high cirrus over the
next 24 hours. There will probably be some patchy ground fog
again on Tuesday morning, but confidence is low that it will
impact the terminals, so left out of the forecast for now. Light
southwest winds will shift west-northwest on Tuesday with the
passage of a weak cold front.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Cobb
AVIATION...Cobb

spc.text:
SPC AC 091954

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0154 PM CST Mon Nov 09 2026

   Valid 092000Z - 101200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Organized severe thunderstorms are not forecast through tonight.

   ...20z Update...
   No changes are needed to the D1 Convective Outlook. See previous
   discussion below for more information.

   ..Halbert-E.. 11/09/2026

   .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1009 AM CST Mon Nov 09 2026/

   ...Synopsis and Discussion...
   Recent satellite imagery shows an elongated upper low centered over
   the TX Big Bend vicinity. Numerous showers and thunderstorms are
   currently ongoing within the broad warm-air advection regime
   downstream of this low from central and south TX across much of the
   TX Coastal Plains into southeast TX. 12Z BRO and CRP soundings
   sampled a seasonally moist airmass characterized by PW values over
   1.8" and poor lapse rates. General expectation is for showers and
   elevated thunderstorms to continue throughout the day while
   diminishing in strength and intensity as an embedded shortwave
   trough continues northeastward. The warm sector, which is
   characterized by upper 60s dewpoints, is forecast to remain largely
   offshore as the associated surface low drifts very slowly eastward. 
   These factors should all act to keep the overall severe weather
   threat very low.

   Guidance also suggests a fast-moving shortwave trough will progress
   through the Pacific Northwest this afternoon/evening, with the
   primary frontal band arriving close to 00Z. Occasional lightning
   flashes may occur with this activity, as mid-level temperatures will
   be fairly cold, but most of the convection should be shallow.
   Enhanced southwesterly flow will exist across the region, but the 
   limited instability and shallow storm depth should limit the risk
   for severe gusts.

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0100Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 091641

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1041 AM CST Mon Nov 09 2026

   Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected Tuesday into early Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   Mid-level impulses will traverse the northern CONUS and the Gulf
   Coast on Tuesday, reinforcing surface high pressure and an
   accompanying stable airmass across most of the CONUS, limiting
   thunderstorm development. A couple of thunderstorms may develop
   along the TX coastline as the Gulf Coast mid-level impulse
   overspreads seasonal moisture. A lightning flash or two may
   accompany impulses across the northwest Washington coastline and
   northern New England. A thunderstorm or two may also develop over
   the central FL Peninsula within a weak warm-air advection regime.
   However, the very sparse thunder coverage precludes general thunder
   highlights over these areas.

   ..Squitieri.. 11/09/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 091929

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0129 PM CST Mon Nov 09 2026

   Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
   OF THE MID MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected Wednesday into early Thursday
   morning.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough will amplify across the eastern half of the CONUS as
   an upper ridge overspreads the U.S. west of the Rockies. Ahead of
   the amplifying upper trough, a surface low will rapidly deepen while
   traversing the OH river through the period, accompanied by a surface
   cold front that will sweep across the Mid-MS Valley. A marginally
   moist airmass will advect northward ahead of the approaching cold
   front, resulting in enough buoyancy (albeit scant), amid strong
   tropospheric flow fields and deep-layer ascent, to support isolated
   strong to potentially severe thunderstorms. 

   ...Mid-MS Valley...
   By late afternoon into early evening, upper 50s F surface dewpoints
   will advect ahead of the surface cold front, amid 7+ C/km mid-level
   lapse rates and minimal MLCINH (per RRFS forecast soundings),
   yielding over 500 J/kg MLCAPE. Given strong forcing for ascent,
   scattered thunderstorms should develop amid a strong unidirectional
   tropospheric wind field by late afternoon into early evening over
   the mid MS Valley. Appreciable strengthening of this flow with
   height should support 50+ kts of effective bulk (speed) shear and
   elongated hodographs. As such, any stronger storm cores that develop
   and become sustained may produce a few damaging gusts, hence the
   introduction of Category 1/Marginal risk probabilities, which is
   also supported by the ML guidance consensus.

   ..Squitieri.. 11/09/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0830Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
